scope: Native BDX stored-byte decoder contract, bounded offline prototype, local loose corpus and two selected structural witnesses; no game/process execution.
decision: Expose a read-only Script inspection view backed by a bounded event-rooted CFG decoder. Numeric bank/index identifies native calls; only SHA-bound known descriptors receive native annotations.

claims.Finding: BDX event lookup scans ID/PC signed32 pairs at script+28, stops on PC0 regardless of ID and returns the first matching ID. ID0 is not intrinsically a terminator.
claims.Limitations: No file-length or duplicate-ID rejection in this native body; offline reader bounds are additional policy.

claims.Finding: The context constructor reads declared allocation fields at script+16/+20/+24 and stores script/context pointers; it may raise header+20 from512 to1024 for five specific names.
claims.Limitations: Offline display reports stored header values, not actual native allocation results or post-load mutated header values.

claims.Finding: Entry initialization stores the supplied PC as a DWORD at context+8 and copies supplied tagged8-byte arguments to the operand stack.
claims.Limitations: Does not validate all subsequent script instructions or resources.

claims.Finding: The interpreter fetches words at script+16+2*PC, dispatches on low4 bits, and implements the complete group-width/control-flow table in opcode-contract.json. Relative calls/branches update a32-bit PC; branch16 sign-extends and call32 combines two words before DWORD addition, without16-bit wrapping.
claims.Limitations: Stored-byte syntactic CFG only. Native memory writes, runtime compatibility adjustments, callback changes, invalid operands and dynamic return stack are not emulated.

claims.Finding: Unary invalid selectors return status5; integer-binary sub>11 instead follows its default pop2/push-left continuation. G9 halt returnsstatus1 with advancedPC, exit returnsstatus2, return restoresPC fromVM stack and returnsstatus3 only for restoredzero.
claims.Limitations: Classification is the captured retail native control flow, not an all-build or safe-execution guarantee.

claims.Finding: Trap groupA reads unsigned bank=word>>6 and unsigned16 index; descriptors stride16. Bank2/index9 and95 decode only when visited as instruction starts from declared event roots.
claims.Limitations: A raw pair8A/9 or8A/5F elsewhere in a payload is not a proven instruction. Native callbacks have unmodeled effects and conditional continuations.

claims.Finding: Address selector helper always consumes one U16 operand. Selectors0..3 resolve frame/work/decoded-object/script-or-scratch forms; others returnNULL.
claims.Limitations: A NULL address pushed through NullableEncode can continue, whereas a load may fault; does not prove argument validity.

claims.Finding: Store helper pops a tagged operand and writes through its supplied destination without a NULL guard on the final stores.
claims.Limitations: Generic native memory writer; malformed script safety and all transitive effects remain outside this inspection task.

claims.Finding: Load helper dereferences its supplied source and pushes the result; no final NULL source guard protects the load.
claims.Limitations: Offline diagnostics do not execute the helper or establish exception handling behavior.

claims.Finding: Nullable pointer encoder preserves a NULL input as zero, which permits the interpreter to push @ADR/0 for unsupported address-selector push forms.
claims.Limitations: Later consumers may still reject or dereference that value; this is not a valid-object assertion.

claims.Finding: Native bank2/index9 adapter maps to411350 and takes three VM operands. Retail-byte-identical B_AL020 type3 script has a decoded instruction atPC6035 on an event0-rooted static CFG path.
claims.Limitations: Original HED/PKG payload and loose slice independently compared byte-for-byte; No observed script execution or operand0 pointer-provenance claim; third argument is unused by adapter body.
